title: Describing things
description: Describe people and things, say 'very' and 'a bit', and compare: bigger than, the best.

guide.title: Adjectives never change
guide.text:
A Bengali adjective has one form only. It does not change for gender, for number or for case: বড় ঘর 'a big room', বড় ঘরগুলো 'the big rooms', বড় মেয়ে 'the elder daughter'.

Before a noun it works as in English: একটা লাল শাড়ি, 'a red sari'. The order is number - adjective - noun.

To say that something IS big, put the adjective after the noun, with no verb: ঘরটা বড়, 'the room (is) big'. The negative uses নয়: ঘরটা বড় নয়.

Some useful pairs: বড় boro big / ছোট chhoto small; ভালো bhaalo good / খারাপ khaaraap bad; নতুন notun new / পুরোনো purono old (of things); গরম gorom hot / ঠান্ডা thaandaa cold; সহজ shohoj easy / কঠিন kothin hard; সস্তা shostaa cheap / দামি daami expensive; লম্বা lombaa long, tall / বেঁটে bente short (of a person).

guide.title: Very, quite, a bit, too
guide.text:
Words of degree go before the adjective.

খুব (khub) very
বেশ (besh) quite, pretty
একটু (ektu) a bit
বেশি (beshi) too, too much - before an adjective (বেশি গরম, 'too hot') or after the thing there is too much of: ঝাল বেশি, 'too spicy'
একদম (ekdom) absolutely
দারুণ (daarun) terrific - used on its own as praise

There is no special word for 'too' as in 'too hot'; খুব গরম or বড্ড গরম (boddo gorom) covers it, or বেশি গরম.

examples.english: The food is a bit spicy.

guide.title: Bigger than, the biggest
guide.text:
Adjectives have no -er or -est forms. To compare, the thing compared WITH takes the possessive ending and is followed by চেয়ে (cheye) 'than'. The adjective is unchanged.

ও আমার চেয়ে বড় - 'he my than big' - He is older (bigger) than me.
এটা ওটার চেয়ে ভালো - This is better than that.

থেকে (theke), 'from', is used in exactly the same way and is very common in speech: আমার থেকে বড়.

You can add আরও (aaro) 'more' or বেশি for emphasis: আরও বড়, 'even bigger'.

The superlative is সবচেয়ে (shobcheye), 'than all': সবচেয়ে ভালো 'the best', সবচেয়ে সস্তা 'the cheapest'.

'Like' is মতো (moto) after a possessive: আমার মতো, 'like me'.

guide.title: Colours
guide.text:
The basic colour words: লাল (laal) red; নীল (neel) blue; সবুজ (shobuj) green; হলুদ (holud) yellow - also the word for turmeric; সাদা (shaadaa) white; কালো (kaalo) black; বাদামি (baadaami) brown; গোলাপি (golaapi) pink; কমলা (komlaa) orange.

'What colour?' is কী রং? (kee rong). 'Colour' itself is রং.

phrases.english: This one is big, that one is small.
phrases.note: Both adjectives keep their final o.

phrases.english: The food is a bit spicy.
phrases.note: ঝাল is chilli-hot; গরম is hot to the touch.
Of people, বড় and ছোট mean older and younger.
